name: Meet Your Team
concept: Recognize the goalkeeper and three lines of teammates, then adjust your midfield role as the ball changes sides.
desc: Recognize the goalkeeper and three lines of teammates, then adjust your midfield role as the ball changes sides.

steps.desc: Your team has seven players: one goalkeeper and six outfield players. Attack toward the goal at the far end.
steps.say: Your team has seven players: one goalkeeper and six outfield players. Attack toward the goal at the far end.

steps.desc: Here, two defenders, three midfielders and one forward start ahead of the keeper. That is two-three-one, or one-two-three-one including the keeper.
steps.say: Here, two defenders, three midfielders and one forward start ahead of the keeper. That is two-three-one, or one-two-three-one including the keeper.

steps.desc: The left defender has the ball. The wide midfielder offers a route ahead; the middle midfielder can help from another angle.
steps.say: The left defender has the ball. The wide midfielder offers a route ahead; the middle midfielder can help from another angle.

steps.desc: You are the middle midfielder. Choose a position that gives the left defender another passing angle.
steps.say: You are the middle midfielder. Choose a position that gives the left defender another passing angle.

steps.desc: Move into the inside angle. Your starting position helps you find a job; you can adjust it as play changes.
steps.say: Move into the inside angle. Your starting position helps you find a job; you can adjust it as play changes.

steps.desc: The defender passes inside. The wide player stays available ahead.
steps.say: The defender passes inside. The wide player stays available ahead.

steps.desc: Return the ball. Now watch the defenders move it to the other side.
steps.say: Return the ball. Now watch the defenders move it to the other side.

steps.desc: The right defender receives. The right midfielder offers width, so your supporting job shifts too.
steps.say: The right defender receives. The right midfielder offers width, so your supporting job shifts too.

steps.desc: You are still the middle midfielder. Choose a useful supporting position for the new passer.
steps.say: You are still the middle midfielder. Choose a useful supporting position for the new passer.

steps.desc: Move across to support. The forward stays higher, while the goalkeeper remains available behind the defenders.
steps.say: Move across to support. The forward stays higher, while the goalkeeper remains available behind the defenders.

steps.desc: The pass reaches you. The same team shape helped on both sides because the players adjusted their positions.
steps.say: The pass reaches you. The same team shape helped on both sides because the players adjusted their positions.

steps.desc: The right defender moves up behind the pass. Starting roles help us share jobs as the ball moves.
steps.say: The right defender moves up behind the pass. Starting roles help us share jobs as the ball moves.

questions.q: Where could the middle midfielder help the player with the ball?
questions.explain: The wide midfielder already offers the outside route. An inside position gives the defender a different option.

spots.why: This creates a separate inside passing angle.
This crowds the route already offered by the wide midfielder.

choiceExplanations: This creates a separate inside passing angle.
This crowds the route already offered by the wide midfielder.

questions.q: Where could the middle midfielder help now?
questions.explain: The ball has changed sides. Moving across gives the right defender an inside option alongside the wide teammate.

spots.why: You are farther from the new passer and give them a longer route.
You give the right defender a closer inside option without crowding the wide player.

choiceExplanations: You are farther from the new passer and give them a longer route.
You give the right defender a closer inside option without crowding the wide player.

name: A Formation Gives Us Options
concept: Use the jobs of the back line, midfield and forward to find a missing wide or supporting option.
desc: Use the jobs of the back line, midfield and forward to find a missing wide or supporting option.

steps.desc: A formation is a starting arrangement. Here, one keeper, two defenders, three midfielders and one forward make one-two-three-one.
steps.say: A formation is a starting arrangement. Here, one keeper, two defenders, three midfielders and one forward make one-two-three-one.

steps.desc: The two defenders give support behind midfield. Without the ball, they protect the route to our goal. The keeper helps behind them.
steps.say: The two defenders give support behind midfield. Without the ball, they protect the route to our goal. The keeper helps behind them.

steps.desc: Three midfielders connect the defenders to the forward. Wide players stretch the team; the middle player offers another passing angle.
steps.say: Three midfielders connect the defenders to the forward. Wide players stretch the team; the middle player offers another passing angle.

steps.desc: The forward gives us a target farther up the field. Everyone still moves to help with the ball and to defend without it.
steps.say: The forward gives us a target farther up the field. Everyone still moves to help with the ball and to defend without it.

steps.desc: Look at our right midfielder. They have drifted close to the middle. The passer needs a route on the right.
steps.say: Look at our right midfielder. They have drifted close to the middle. The passer needs a route on the right.

steps.desc: You are the right midfielder. Which move adds the option our shape is missing?
steps.say: You are the right midfielder. Which move adds the option our shape is missing?

steps.desc: Move wide enough to offer a different angle. You can leave your starting spot when the game needs it.
steps.say: Move wide enough to offer a different angle. You can leave your starting spot when the game needs it.

steps.desc: The middle player passes wide. Now the midfield and back line must keep helping the new ball carrier.
steps.say: The middle player passes wide. Now the midfield and back line must keep helping the new ball carrier.

steps.desc: A defender closes the forward route. The middle player has run ahead too, so the ball carrier needs help behind.
steps.say: A defender closes the forward route. The middle player has run ahead too, so the ball carrier needs help behind.

steps.desc: Our forward still offers height. The right defender is deeper; a closer midfield angle can connect the team.
steps.say: Our forward still offers height. The right defender is deeper; a closer midfield angle can connect the team.

steps.desc: You are the middle midfielder now. Which move gives the wide teammate a clear return?
steps.say: You are the middle midfielder now. Which move gives the wide teammate a clear return?

steps.desc: Drop behind and inside. A midfielder can help from different heights as the picture changes.
steps.say: Drop behind and inside. A midfielder can help from different heights as the picture changes.

steps.desc: The return reaches midfield. Width, a player ahead and support behind give the team choices.
steps.say: The return reaches midfield. Width, a player ahead and support behind give the team choices.

steps.desc: One-three-two-one is another possible formation: three defenders, two midfielders and one forward. Neither set of numbers fixes players to the grass.
steps.say: One-three-two-one is another possible formation: three defenders, two midfielders and one forward. Neither set of numbers fixes players to the grass.

steps.desc: Try different positions in practice. Explain who can help ahead, beside and behind you before choosing where to move.
steps.say: Try different positions in practice. Explain who can help ahead, beside and behind you before choosing where to move.

spots.why: This restores a wide option on the right.

name: Goal Kick & Build-Out Line · AYSO
concept: AYSO rule example, checked September 2026: recognize the build-out boundary and when pressure may resume after a goal kick.
desc: AYSO rule example, checked September 2026: recognize the build-out boundary and when pressure may resume after a goal kick.

steps.desc: This example uses AYSO build-out rules. Other competitions can use different rules; the shared idea is making room to restart and helping the keeper.
steps.say: This example uses AYSO build-out rules. Other competitions can use different rules; the shared idea is making room to restart and helping the keeper.

steps.desc: Our team has a goal kick. The dashed line across our half sits halfway between the penalty area and the halfway line.
steps.say: Our team has a goal kick. The dashed line across our half sits halfway between the penalty area and the halfway line.

steps.desc: Before this goal kick, where must the blue player move to give our team room?
steps.say: Before this goal kick, where must the blue player move to give our team room?

steps.desc: Blue retreats beyond the line. Our defenders offer routes on either side while the keeper prepares the stationary ball.
steps.say: Blue retreats beyond the line. Our defenders offer routes on either side while the keeper prepares the stationary ball.

steps.desc: A goal kick may go short or beyond the line. Here the left defender is available. Pressure can return once the ball is kicked and clearly moves.
steps.say: A goal kick may go short or beyond the line. Here the left defender is available. Pressure can return once the ball is kicked and clearly moves.

steps.desc: The keeper kicks to the left defender. The ball is now in play; blue does not have to wait for the receiver to touch it.
steps.say: The keeper kicks to the left defender. The ball is now in play; blue does not have to wait for the receiver to touch it.

steps.desc: The kick has been taken. Blue can now cross the line, even though the ball stayed on our side of it.
steps.say: The kick has been taken. Blue can now cross the line, even though the ball stayed on our side of it.

steps.desc: The same blue player has a new choice now. Does the line still keep them back?
steps.say: The same blue player has a new choice now. Does the line still keep them back?

steps.desc: Blue approaches the receiver. Our middle player offers a new angle, because the protected restart has become open play.
steps.say: Blue approaches the receiver. Our middle player offers a new angle, because the protected restart has become open play.

steps.desc: The defender passes to midfield before the pressure arrives. Support must continue after the restart.
steps.say: The defender passes to midfield before the pressure arrives. Support must continue after the restart.

steps.desc: The keeper may also restart quickly before every opponent retreats, accepting the risk of interception. Waiting gives teammates time to find space.
steps.say: The keeper may also restart quickly before every opponent retreats, accepting the risk of interception. Waiting gives teammates time to find space.

steps.desc: With the ball held in the keeper’s hands, AYSO also requires retreat. Release from the hands lets opponents cross; an ordinary pass back in open play does not create that protection.
steps.say: With the ball held in the keeper’s hands, AYSO also requires retreat. Release from the hands lets opponents cross; an ordinary pass back in open play does not create that protection.

steps.desc: In this AYSO profile the far build-out line also changes the offside boundary. This lesson teaches the goal kick; check your competition before applying these rules.
steps.say: In this AYSO profile the far build-out line also changes the offside boundary. This lesson teaches the goal kick; check your competition before applying these rules.

steps.desc: The midfielder carries into the available angle. The left defender moves up behind to stay connected after the restart.
steps.say: The midfielder carries into the available angle. The left defender moves up behind to stay connected after the restart.

catalog.name: Goal Kick & Build-Out Line · AYSO
catalog.what: AYSO rule example, checked September 2026: recognize the build-out boundary and when pressure may resume after a goal kick.

questions.q: Where must the blue player retreat before the goal kick?
options: Behind the build-out line, toward halfway
questions.explain: For this AYSO goal kick, opponents must retreat behind the build-out line. The ball is still stationary.

spots.why: This is beyond the line, away from the goal being restarted.
This stays inside the protected area and moves closer to the keeper.

choiceExplanations: This is beyond the line, away from the goal being restarted.
This stays inside the protected area and moves closer to the keeper.

questions.q: After the goal kick clearly moves, what may blue do?
options: Stay behind the line until the ball crosses it
Cross the line to approach the ball
questions.explain: Under this AYSO profile, the kicked and clearly moving ball releases the opponents. The receiver does not need to touch it first.

spots.why: Waiting is a tactical choice, but the rule no longer requires it.
Blue may cross now because the goal kick has put the ball in play.

choiceExplanations: Waiting is a tactical choice, but the rule no longer requires it.
Blue may cross now because the goal kick has put the ball in play.

name: Look, Then Turn or Return
concept: Look for pressure before receiving. Turn into room or give the ball back.
desc: Look for pressure before receiving. Turn into room or give the ball back.

steps.desc: Before the pass arrives, look over your shoulder. Where is the defender?
steps.say: Before the pass arrives, look over your shoulder. Where is the defender?

steps.desc: The pass reaches your feet. Keep your body open so you can see ahead.
steps.say: The pass reaches your feet. Keep your body open so you can see ahead.

steps.desc: There is room in front of you. A small touch can take you into it.
steps.say: There is room in front of you. A small touch can take you into it.

steps.desc: Turn with the ball close. You can look up again as you move.
steps.say: Turn with the ball close. You can look up again as you move.

steps.desc: Send it back and try another picture. Watch how the defender changes position.
steps.say: Send it back and try another picture. Watch how the defender changes position.

steps.desc: Check back toward the passer. This time the defender follows you.
steps.say: Check back toward the passer. This time the defender follows you.

steps.desc: Receive with the defender close in front. You still have help behind.
steps.say: Receive with the defender close in front. You still have help behind.

steps.desc: You do not have to turn every time. Keep the ball away from pressure.
steps.say: You do not have to turn every time. Keep the ball away from pressure.

steps.desc: Give it back. You kept possession because you noticed the pressure.
steps.say: Give it back. You kept possession because you noticed the pressure.

steps.desc: The defender takes the return away from pressure. The midfielder moves to offer another angle instead of staying beside the opponent.
steps.say: The defender takes the return away from pressure. The midfielder moves to offer another angle instead of staying beside the opponent.

steps.say: The left teammate is close to the defender. There is more room near the side.
